source_text: Ἀπελογησάμεθα οὖν κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν ἡμῖν ὡς ἐν τοιούτῳ συγγράμματι πρὸς τὸ ἐχρῆν, εἴπερ ὄντως ἐκφῆναι θείαν δύναμιν ἤθελεν, αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἐπηρεάσασι καὶ τῷ καταδικάσαντι καὶ ὅλως πᾶσιν ὀφθῆναι. οὐκ ἐχρῆν οὖν τῷ καταδικάσαντι αὐτὸν ὀφθῆναι οὐδὲ τοῖς ἐπηρεάσασιν. ἐφείδετο γὰρ καὶ τοῦ καταδικάσαντος καὶ τῶν ἐπηρεασάντων ὁ Ἰησοῦς. ἵνα μὴ παταχθῶσιν „ἀορασίᾳ,“ ὁποίᾳ οἱ ἐν Σοδόμοις ἐπατάχθησαν, ἡνίκα ἐπεβούλευον τῇ ὥρᾳ τῶν ξενισθέντων παρὰ τῷ Λὼτ ἀγγέλων. καὶ τοῦτο δὲ δηλοῦται διὰ τούτων· „ἐκτείναντες δὲ οἱ ἄνδρες τὰς χεῖρας ἐσπάσαντο τὸν Λὼτ πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς εἰς τὸν οἶκον, καὶ τὴν θύραν ἀπέκλεισαν· τοὺς δὲ ἄνδρας τοὺς ἐπὶ τῇ θύρᾳ τοῦ οἴκου ἐπάταξαν ἀορασίᾳ ἀπὸ μικροῦ ἕως μεγάλου· καὶ παρελύθησαν ζητοῦντες τὴν θύραν.“ ἐκφῆναι οὖν ἐβούλετο τὴν δύναμιν ἑαυτοῦ ὁ Ἰησοῦς θείαν οὖσαν ἑκάστῳ τῶν δυναμένων αὐτὴν ἰδεῖν, καὶ κατὰ τὸ μέτρον ἰδεῖν ἃ ἐχώρει. καὶ οὐ δή που δι᾿ ἄλλο ἐφυλάξατο ὀφθῆναι ἢ διὰ τὰς δυνάμεις τῶν μὴ χωρούντων αὐτὸν ἰδεῖν. καὶ μάτην παρελήφθη τῷ Κέλσῳ τὸ οὐ γὰρ δὴ ἔτι ἐφοβεῖτό τινα ἀνθρώπων ἀποθανὼν καὶ, ὥς φατε, θεὸς ὢν, οὐδ᾿ ἐπὶ τοῦτ᾿ ἐπέμφθη τὴν ἀρχὴν, ἵνα λάθῃ. ἐπέμφθη γὰρ οὐ μόνον. ἵνα γνωσθῇ, ἀλλ᾿ ἵνα καὶ λάθῃ, οὐ γὰρ πᾶν, ὃ ἦν, καὶ οἷς ἐγινώσκετο ἐγινώσκετο. ἀλλά τι αὐτοῦ ἐλάνθανεν αὐτούς· τισὶ δ᾿ οὐδ᾿ ὅλως ἐγινώσκετο. καὶ ἀνέῳξε δὲ „φωτὸς“ πύλας τοῖς γενομένοις μὲν „σκότους“ καὶ „νυκτὸς“ υἱοῖς, ἐπιδεδωκόσι δὲ ἑαυτοὺς εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι υἱοὺς „ἡμέρας“ καὶ „φωτός.“ καὶ ἦλθε σωτὴρ ὁ κύριος ἡμῖν μᾶλλον ὡς ἰατρὸς ἀγαθὸς τοῖς ἁμαρτιῶν μεστοῖς ἢ τοῖς δικαίοις.
pass_a_gloss: We made defence (ἀπελογησάμεθα), then, according to what is possible (τὸ δυνατόν) for us as in such a treatise (σύγγραμμα), against the [words] 'it was necessary (ἐχρῆν), if he really (ὄντως) wished (ἤθελεν) to reveal (ἐκφῆναι) divine power (δύναμις), to be seen by those very men who insulted/abused (ἐπηρεάσασι) [him] and by the one who condemned (καταδικάσαντι) [him] and wholly (ὅλως) by all.' It was not necessary, then, to be seen by the one who condemned him nor by those who abused. For Jesus was sparing (ἐφείδετο) both the condemner and the abusers, that they might not be struck (παταχθῶσιν) with 'blindness (ἀορασία)', such as those in Sodom were struck with, when they were plotting against (ἐπεβούλευον) the bloom/beauty (ὥρα) of the angels lodged as guests (ξενισθέντων) with Lot. And this is shown through these: 'And the men, stretching out their hands, drew (ἐσπάσαντο) Lot to themselves into the house, and shut (ἀπέκλεισαν) the door; and the men at the door of the house they struck with blindness from small to great; and they were exhausted (παρελύθησαν) seeking the door.' So Jesus wished to reveal his power, being divine, to each of those able to see it, and according to the measure (μέτρον) to see the things which [each] contained (ἐχώρει). And surely (δή που) for no other [reason] he guarded himself against (ἐφυλάξατο) being seen than because of the capacities (δυνάμεις) of those not containing (μὴ χωρούντων) to see him. And in vain (μάτην) was taken up (παρελήφθη) by Celsus the [saying]: 'For indeed he no longer feared (ἐφοβεῖτο) any of men, having died and, as you say (φατε), being God, nor was he sent (ἐπέμφθη) at the beginning (τὴν ἀρχήν) for this, that he might escape notice (λάθῃ).' For he was sent not only that he might be known (γνωσθῇ), but that he might also escape notice; for not all that he was was known even by those to whom he was known, but something of him escaped (ἐλάνθανεν) them; and to some he was not known at all (οὐδ᾿ ὅλως). And he opened (ἀνέῳξε) gates (πύλαι) of 'light' to those who had become sons of 'darkness (σκότος)' and 'night (νύξ)', but had given themselves (ἐπιδεδωκόσι ἑαυτούς) toward becoming sons of 'day (ἡμέρα)' and 'light'. And the Lord came (ἦλθε) as Saviour (σωτήρ) for us, rather (μᾶλλον) as a good physician (ἰατρὸς ἀγαθός) to those full (μεστοῖς) of sins than to the righteous (δίκαιοι).
pass_b_english: We have answered, then, as far as we could in a work of this kind, the claim: “If he really wished to display divine power, he ought to have appeared to the very men who had abused him, and to the one who condemned him, and in short to all.” He ought not, then, to have appeared to the one who condemned him, nor to those who had abused him. For Jesus was sparing both the one who condemned him and those who had abused him, so that they might not be struck with “blindness,” as the men of Sodom were struck when they plotted against the beauty of the angels who were guests in Lot’s house. This is made plain by these words: “The men stretched out their hands and drew Lot into the house to them, and shut the door; and they struck the men who were at the door of the house with blindness, from small to great, and they wore themselves out looking for the door” (Genesis 19:10–11).

So Jesus wished to display his power, which was divine, to each of those able to see it, and in the measure of what each could take in. Surely it was for no other reason that he took care not to be seen than out of regard for the capacities of those who could not take in the sight of him.

And Celsus brings this in to no purpose: “For he certainly no longer feared any man, once he had died and was, as you say, God; nor was he sent in the first place for this, to stay hidden.” For he was sent not only to be known but also to stay hidden. For even those who knew him did not know all that he was; something of him escaped them, and to some he was not known at all. And he opened the gates of “light” to those who had been sons of “darkness” and “night,” but who had given themselves to becoming sons of “the day” and of “light” (1 Thessalonians 5:5). And the Lord came to us as Saviour, as a good physician, to those full of sins rather than to the righteous (Matthew 9:12–13).

choices.why: αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἐπηρεάσασι: added 'the very men' in Celsus's restated claim.
μὴ χωρούντων αὐτὸν ἰδεῖν: 'could not bear to see him' -> 'could not take in the sight of him'.
Restored 'For' (γάρ) at 'For not all that he was'.

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; English is from the Greek.

revisions.note: 'For not all that he was was known even to those by whom he was known' recast in the active, 'For even those who knew him did not know all that he was' (2026-10-24), because the output guard reads 'was was' as a doubled word. Same sense of οὐ γὰρ πᾶν, ὃ ἦν, καὶ οἷς ἐγινώσκετο ἐγινώσκετο.

notes: Translated from the Greek of the staged Koetschau row only; Crombie (ANF) and Chadwick were not used.

translator_notes: The opening claim repeats Celsus’s words from 2.63 (‘ἐχρῆν... ὀφθῆναι’); the Greek introduces them only with ‘πρὸς τὸ’ (against the words), so no speaker label is added beyond ‘the claim’. ‘τῇ ὥρᾳ’ rendered ‘the beauty’ (ὥρα in the sense of youthful bloom), not ‘the hour’. ‘ἀορασία’ (blindness) is the LXX word of Genesis 19:11; the quotation is LXX Genesis 19:10-11 (‘παρελύθησαν ζητοῦντες’, they wore themselves out looking). ‘διὰ τὰς δυνάμεις τῶν μὴ χωρούντων’ rendered ‘out of regard for the capacities’: δυνάμεις here means the limited powers of the viewers, not miracles. Celsus’s sentence is set in double quotation marks; ‘θεὸς ὤν, ὥς φατε’ is Celsus reporting the Christian claim, rendered ‘God’ since it names the Christian belief that Jesus is God. ‘ἵνα λάθῃ’ rendered ‘to stay hidden’ (lit. escape notice) in both Celsus’s and Origen’s clauses, so Origen’s turn of Celsus’s word stays visible. ‘sons of light... day... night... darkness’ is a clear allusion to 1 Thessalonians 5:5. The physician saying alludes to Matthew 9:12-13 (compare Mark 2:17; Luke 5:31-32); not a quotation. ‘ἦλθε σωτὴρ ὁ κύριος ἡμῖν μᾶλλον ὡς ἰατρὸς ἀγαθὸς τοῖς ἁμαρτιῶν μεστοῖς ἢ τοῖς δικαίοις’ rendered with ‘rather than’ governing ‘those full of sins’ vs ‘the righteous’.

'For not all that he was was known even to those by whom he was known' recast in the active, 'For even those who knew him did not know all that he was' (2026-10-24), because the output guard reads 'was was' as a doubled word. Same sense of οὐ γὰρ πᾶν, ὃ ἦν, καὶ οἷς ἐγινώσκετο ἐγινώσκετο.
